full_judgment:
Md. Mozammel Hoque J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 27.5.84 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 952 of 1981 decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff. 

 3. It is further stated by the plaintiff that house Nos. 371, 372 and 127 Elephant Road, Dhaka, house No. 132, New Eskaton, Dhaka and a shop at 1, Jail Road, Dhaka were the properties of Ferdous Tannery, but the same were not included in the schedule of the agreement executed between the parties on 25.8.78. The schedule of the agreement contains all other properties of Ferdous Tannery excepting the aforesaid 5 houses. Since the aforesaid five properties, though belong to the Ferdous Tannery, were not included in the agreement, the plaintiff had to file the present suit for declaration of title. It is the case of the plaintiff that all the aforesaid five properties are the assets of the M/s. Ferdous Tannery which was sold with all its assets to the plaintiff through tender. It should be declared that the aforesaid five properties are the assets of Ferdous Tannery and as such the plaintiff is entitled to a decree as he is the purchaser of Ferdous Tannery along with its all assets wherever situated. 

 "(aa). to pass a decree for specific performance of contract directing the defendants to execute and register the sale deed transferring the suit properties in favour of the plaintiff within a time to be fixed by the Court and also to deliver possession of the suit properties to the plaintiff and in case of failure to do so the Court may be pleased to execute and register on behalf of the defendant and also.to deliver possession of the same through the process of law." 

 8. Plaintiff examined 2 witnesses and the defendant also examined 2 witnesses in support of their respective case. Both the parties adduced some documents and papers which have been duly marked as exhibits. After considering the materials on record and hearing the parties, the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit on 27.5.84. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree, the present defendant-appellants preferred this First Appeal. 

 16. In order to consider the submissions of Dr. Zahir, let us now consider the deed of agreement for sale (Ext. C) itself. In the deed, the plaintiff is the purchaser and the President of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is the seller. In the preamble of Ext. C it is stipulated that whereas the seller agreed to sell to the purchaser for a total consideration of Tk. 40,50,000/- the industrial unit M/s Ferdous Tannery located at Hazaribagh, PS Mohammadpur, District Dhaka having its principal office of business at Hazaribagh, PS Mohammadpur, Dhaka, "together with its existing assets" and liabilities of Taka nil with Bangladesh Shilpa Bank, Shilpa Rin Sangstha, Commercial Bank being the balance amount of the long term loan taken by the said industrial unit, "as fully described in the schedule 1," hereunder collectively termed as the demised property. In this deed of agreement other terms and conditions in respect of sale of the said properties are in no way disputed. From the document itself it appears to us that it was signed by both the parties and no objection was raised in any form whatsoever and this industrial unit, namely, M/s Ferdous Tannery together with its existing assets as described in the deed of agreement have been agreed to be sold to the plaintiff. This is very clear and unambiguous and there is no room for any doubt or misunderstanding in the preamble and schedule of the agreement. The plaintiff is claiming that the properties situated at 127, 371 and 372 Elephant Road, Dhaka, 132 New Eskaton, Dhaka and 1, Jail Road, Dhaka are also the properties of Ferdous Tannery and as such the plaintiff is entitled to those properties inasmuch as the plaintiff purchased all assets of Ferdous Tannaery situated anywhere in Bangladesh. But we find that the aforesaid properties do not find any place in the schedule 1 of the aforesaid agreement, Ext. C. In view of sections 91 and 94 of the Evidence Act, we find that the plaintiff is not entitled to go beyond the agreement made by himself and the government. The Ext. C, the deed of agreement, shall have to be considered in its true plain meaning without bringing any other extraneous consideration. The tender notice, Ext. 11, does not show that the aforesaid five properties were the properties of Ferdous Tannery and the industrial concern, namely, Ferdous Tannery, would be sold along with the aforesaid five properties. In the deed of agreement, we also find that without raising any objection the plaintiff accepted the terms and conditions of the agreement and both the parties signed it. Since it is a suit for declaration as well as specific performance of contract, the parties must go by the terms of the contract. Parties in the contract are bound to fulfil the terms of the contract specifically. If they fail to do so, the Court will pass a decree for specific performance of contract. In the present suit, it appears that the aforesaid five properties were not the subject matter of the contract and there is no term laid down in the contract that the defendants are bound to sell those five properties along with the industrial unit M/s Ferdous Tannery. In this view of the matter, we find that there is no failure on the part of the defendants to perform or to fulfil any terms of the contract. Rather, in the written statement, the defendants case is that whatever was agreed between the parties in the deed of agreement, they are willing to fulfil all the terms and conditions and in fact the defendants have delivered possession of all the properties which have found place in the contract itself. So, we find substance in the contention of Dr. Zahir. 

 21. Since the plaintiff has failed to show that the government had the intention to sell the aforesaid five properties along with the Industrial unit M/s Ferdous Tannery and since the agreement itself is very clear and free from any ambiguity we are of the view that the present suit for specific performance of contract by the plaintiff is not maintainable inasmuch as the defendants are not bound to sell the aforesaid five properties in pursuance of the terms and conditions made in the agreement for sale, namely, Ext. C. The properties described in the schedule of the agreement Ext. C are not disputed by the defendants and the defendants are ready to execute and register the sale deed for those properties as it appears from the records. Regard being had to the facts and circumstance of the case and the material evidence on record,we hold that the plaintiff is not entitled to have a decree in the form of title and specific performance of contract in respect of the aforesaid five properties and as such the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court cannot be sustained in law. 

 22. In the result, this appeal is allowed and the judgment and decree of the Trial Court are hereby set aside and the suit for declaration of title and for specific performance of contract is dismissed.
